name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.torsFin
source: ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (D : Type) [AddCommGroup D] [Module ℤ_[l] D], Module.Finite ℤ_[l] (D →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) →
haveI : Fact (1 < l ^ 1) := ⟨by rw [pow_one]; exact hl.one_lt⟩
set Q : Set (QZ l) := {q | (l : ℤ_[l]) • q = 0} with hQ
have h0 : ι 1 = ι 0 := by rw [h, map_zero]
have hsep : ∀ t : D, (l : ℤ_[l]) • t = 0 → (∀ g ∈ s, g t = 0) → t = 0 := by
have hall : LinearMap.applyₗ (R := ℤ_[l]) (M₂ := QZ l) t = 0 :=
LinearMap.ext_on hs (fun g hg' => by simpa using hg g hg')
let μt : ℤ_[l] →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] D := LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℤ_[l] D t
let ν : ℤ_[l] →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l := LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℤ_[l] (QZ l) (ι 1)
have hker : LinearMap.ker μt ≤ LinearMap.ker ν := by
have ha' : a • t = 0 := by simpa [μt] using ha
· have hm : a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[l] := (IsLocalRing.mem_maximalIdeal a).mpr hu
let g0 : LinearMap.range μt →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l :=
obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (qzInj l).out (LinearMap.range μt).subtype Subtype.val_injective g0
have hmem : μt 1 ∈ LinearMap.range μt := LinearMap.mem_range_self μt 1
have h3 : (LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange μt).symm ⟨μt 1, hmem⟩ = Submodule.Quotient.mk 1 := by
have h2 : g0 ⟨μt 1, hmem⟩ = ι 1 := by
let f : D → (s → QZ l) := fun φ g => (g : D →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) φ
have hpi : (Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ : s => Q)).Finite := Set.Finite.pi (fun _ => hQfin)
show (l : ℤ_[l]) • (g : D →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) φ = 0
rw [← map_smul, show (l : ℤ_[l]) • φ = 0 from hφ, map_zero]
· intro φ hφ ψ hψ hfe
have := hsep (φ - ψ) (by rw [smul_sub, hφ', hψ', sub_zero]) (fun g hg => by
show: If the ℓ-adic linear character dual of a module D is finitely generated, the subgroup of elements of D killed by ℓ is finite.
strategy: Evaluate at a finite family of generators of the dual. On the ℓ-torsion these evaluations take only finitely many values. Injectivity of the character module makes them separate points.

steps.claim: By hypothesis $\ell$ is prime, so the residue ring modulo $\ell$ has at least two elements. Write $T=\mathbf Q_\ell/\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $D^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(D,T)$.
At level one there is an injective additive map $\iota:\mathbf Z/\ell^1\mathbf Z\hookrightarrow T$ whose image consists precisely of the elements killed by $\ell^1$.
The modulus $\ell^1$ is nonzero because the prime $\ell$ is nonzero.
Since $\ell^1=\ell>1$, the classes of zero and one modulo $\ell^1$ are distinct.
steps.snippet: haveI : Fact (1 < l ^ 1) := ⟨by rw [pow_one]; exact hl.one_lt⟩

steps.claim: Put $Q=T[\ell]=\{q\in T\mid \ell q=0\}$. For every $\varphi\in D[\ell]$, linearity places every character value at $\varphi$ in $Q$.
steps.snippet: set Q : Set (QZ l) := {q | (l : ℤ_[l]) • q = 0} with hQ

steps.claim: The set $Q$ is finite because it is the image of the finite residue group under $\iota$.

children.claim: An element of $T$ belongs to $Q$ exactly when it lies in the image of $\iota$, by the description at exponent one.
children.snippet:
have : Q = Set.range ι := by
      ext q
      rw [hιrange q, pow_one]
      rfl

children.claim: The domain of $\iota$ is finite, so its image, already identified with $Q$, is finite as well.
children.snippet:
rw [this]
    exact Set.finite_range ι

steps.claim: Put $q_1=\iota(1)$. This element of $T$ is nonzero because $\iota$ is injective and $1\ne0$ in its domain.
steps.snippet:
have hι1 : ι 1 ≠ 0 := by
    intro h

children.claim: If $q_1=0$, then $\iota(1)=\iota(0)$ because the additive map $\iota$ sends zero to zero.
children.snippet: have h0 : ι 1 = ι 0 := by rw [h, map_zero]

children.claim: The supposed equality $\iota(1)=\iota(0)$ gives $1=0$ by injectivity, contradicting the nontriviality of $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$.
children.snippet:
have := hιinj h0
    exact one_ne_zero this

steps.claim: The element $q_1$ is killed by $\ell$ because it belongs to the image of $\iota$.
steps.snippet:
have hlι : (l : ℤ_[l]) • ι 1 = 0 := by
    have := (hιrange (ι 1)).mp ⟨1, rfl⟩
    simpa using this

steps.claim: Choose a finite set $s$ spanning the entire character module $D^\vee$ over $\mathbf Z_\ell$, using its finite generation.

For $t\in D[\ell]$, vanishing of all the characters in $s$ at $t$ forces $t=0$. Indeed, spanning then forces every character to vanish there, while a nonzero $t$ admits a character with value $q_1\ne0$ by extension from $\mathbf Z_\ell t$.
steps.snippet:
have hsep : ∀ t : D, (l : ℤ_[l]) • t = 0 → (∀ g ∈ s, g t = 0) → t = 0 := by
    intro t htl hg

children.claim: Evaluation $D^\vee\to T$ at $t$ is zero because it is linear and agrees with zero on all generators in $s$.
children.snippet:
have hall : LinearMap.applyₗ (R := ℤ_[l]) (M₂ := QZ l) t = 0 :=
      LinearMap.ext_on hs (fun g hg' => by simpa using hg g hg')

children.claim: Suppose $t\ne0$. Define $\mu_t:\mathbf Z_\ell\to D$ by $a\mapsto at$ and $\nu:\mathbf Z_\ell\to T$ by $a\mapsto aq_1$. Their images contain $t$ and $q_1$, respectively, as the values at $1$.
Every scalar annihilating $t$ annihilates $q_1$. It cannot be a unit since $t\ne0$, so it is a multiple of $\ell$, which kills $q_1$.
children.snippet:
have hker : LinearMap.ker μt ≤ LinearMap.ker ν := by
      intro a ha

children.claim: From $\mu_t(a)=0$ and the definition of $\mu_t$ we obtain $at=0$.
children.snippet: have ha' : a • t = 0 := by simpa [μt] using ha

children.claim: Membership in $\ker\nu$ is exactly the equality $aq_1=0$.
children.snippet: show a • ι 1 = 0

children.claim: Since $t\ne0$, a scalar $a$ with $at=0$ cannot be a unit. Every such $a$ lies in the maximal ideal $(\ell)$ of $\mathbf Z_\ell$, and this ideal kills $q_1$.
children.snippet: by_cases hu : IsUnit a

children.claim: If $a$ is invertible, multiplying $at=0$ by $a^{-1}$ gives $t=0$, contrary to the chosen nonzero point.
children.snippet: · exact absurd ((hu.smul_eq_zero).mp ha') ht

children.claim: If $a$ is a nonunit, $a$ belongs to the maximal ideal $(\ell)$, so $a=b\ell$ for some $b\in\mathbf Z_\ell$. Since $\ell q_1=0$, this gives $aq_1=0$.
children.snippet: · have hm : a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[l] := (IsLocalRing.mem_maximalIdeal a).mpr hu

children.claim: Every nonunit of the local ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$ belongs to its maximal ideal, so $a\in\mathfrak m_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ in this branch.
children.snippet: · have hm : a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[l] := (IsLocalRing.mem_maximalIdeal a).mpr hu

children.claim: The maximal ideal of $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is generated by $\ell$. Writing $a=b\ell$ therefore gives $a q_1=b(\ell q_1)=0$.
children.snippet:
rw [PadicInt.maximalIdeal_eq_span_p, Ideal.mem_span_singleton'] at hm
        obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hm
        rw [mul_smul, hlι, smul_zero]

children.claim: The kernel inclusion lets $\nu$ descend through $\mathbf Z_\ell/\ker\mu_t\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell t$, giving $g_0(at)=a q_1$. Injectivity of $T$ over $\mathbf Z_\ell$ extends $g_0$ from the cyclic submodule to a character $y$ on all of $D$.
The element $\mu_t(1)$ lies in $\operatorname{im}\mu_t$, with $1$ itself a preimage.
children.snippet: have hmem : μt 1 ∈ LinearMap.range μt := LinearMap.mem_range_self μt 1

children.claim: The quotient-to-image isomorphism sends the class of $1$ to $\mu_t(1)$ by definition. Its inverse therefore sends this image element back to the class of $1$.
children.snippet:
have h3 : (LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange μt).symm ⟨μt 1, hmem⟩ = Submodule.Quotient.mk 1 := by
      rw [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq]
      rfl

children.claim: The defining agreement of $y$ with $g_0$ gives $y(\mu_t(1))=g_0(\mu_t(1))$.
children.snippet: have h1 := hy ⟨μt 1, hmem⟩

children.claim: The descended map takes $\mu_t(1)$ to $q_1$, since the representative $1$ has value $\nu(1)=q_1$.
children.snippet:
have h2 : g0 ⟨μt 1, hmem⟩ = ι 1 := by
      simp only [g0, LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, Function.comp_apply]
      rw [h3, Submodule.liftQ_apply]
      simp [ν]

children.claim: Substituting this computed value into the extension equality yields $y(\mu_t(1))=q_1$.
children.snippet: rw [h2] at h1

children.claim: Every character vanishes at $t$ because evaluation there is zero. In particular $y(t)=0$.
children.snippet:
have hyt : y t = 0 := by
      have := LinearMap.congr_fun hall y
      simpa using this

children.claim: The scalar map satisfies $\mu_t(1)=1t=t$.
children.snippet: have : μt 1 = t := by simp [μt]

children.claim: Now $y(t)=q_1$ by the extension equality and $\mu_t(1)=t$, but evaluation at $t$ gave $y(t)=0$. Since $q_1\ne0$, the supposition $t\ne0$ is impossible.
children.snippet:
simp only [Submodule.coe_subtype, this] at h1
    exact hι1 (h1 ▸ hyt)

steps.claim: Define $f:D\to T^s$ by $f(\varphi)_g=g(\varphi)$. Its coordinates are the evaluations at the chosen generators of $D^\vee$.
steps.snippet: let f : D → (s → QZ l) := fun φ g => (g : D →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) φ

steps.claim: The set $Q^s$ of tuples with every coordinate in $T[\ell]$ is finite because both $s$ and $Q$ are finite.
steps.snippet: have hpi : (Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ : s => Q)).Finite := Set.Finite.pi (fun _ => hQfin)

steps.claim: Evaluation identifies $D[\ell]$ with its image in the finite product $Q^s$. Each coordinate of a point in $D[\ell]$ lies in $Q$, and equal tuples for $\varphi,\psi\in D[\ell]$ force every generator in $s$ to vanish at $\varphi-\psi$. The separation property gives $\varphi=\psi$, so $D[\ell]$ is finite.

children.claim: For $\varphi\in D[\ell]$ and $g\in s$, linearity gives $\ell g(\varphi)=g(\ell\varphi)=0$. Thus $f(D[\ell])$ lies in the finite set $Q^s$ and is finite.
children.snippet: · apply hpi.subset

children.claim: An element of $f(D[\ell])$ is $f(\varphi)$ for some $\varphi$ with $\ell\varphi=0$. For each $g\in s$ its coordinate $g(\varphi)$ lies in $Q$, since $\ell g(\varphi)=g(\ell\varphi)=0$.
children.snippet:
· apply hpi.subset
    rintro _ ⟨φ, hφ, rfl⟩ g _

children.claim: Membership of this coordinate in $Q$ amounts to $\ell g(\varphi)=0$.
children.snippet: show (l : ℤ_[l]) • (g : D →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) φ = 0

children.claim: For every coordinate, linearity gives $\ell g(\varphi)=g(\ell\varphi)=g(0)=0$ because $\varphi$ lies in $D[\ell]$.
children.snippet: rw [← map_smul, show (l : ℤ_[l]) • φ = 0 from hφ, map_zero]

children.claim: The equality $\ell\varphi=0$ is the defining condition for the chosen $\varphi$ to belong to $D[\ell]$.
children.snippet: rw [← map_smul, show (l : ℤ_[l]) • φ = 0 from hφ, map_zero]

children.claim: Suppose $\varphi,\psi\in D[\ell]$ have equal evaluation tuples. Then $\ell(\varphi-\psi)=0$, and each $g\in s$ takes the value zero on $\varphi-\psi$. Separation forces $\varphi-\psi=0$, proving the required injectivity.
children.snippet: · intro φ hφ ψ hψ hfe

children.claim: Membership of $\varphi$ in $D[\ell]$ gives $\ell\varphi=0$.
children.snippet: have hφ' : (l : ℤ_[l]) • φ = 0 := hφ

children.claim: The second point $\psi$ belongs to $D[\ell]$, so it satisfies $\ell\psi=0$.
children.snippet: have hψ' : (l : ℤ_[l]) • ψ = 0 := hψ

children.claim: Equality of the tuples yields $g(\varphi)=g(\psi)$ in every coordinate, so $g(\varphi-\psi)=0$ by linearity. Also $\ell(\varphi-\psi)=\ell\varphi-\ell\psi=0$. Separation now shows $\varphi=\psi$.
children.snippet:
have := hsep (φ - ψ) (by rw [smul_sub, hφ', hψ', sub_zero]) (fun g hg => by
      have := congr_fun hfe ⟨g, hg⟩
      simp only [f] at this
      rw [map_sub, this, sub_self])
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp this
